subject: Realtime stream surge: interim triage, recommended client mitigations, and remediation plan
summary: Customer reported periodic high-latency spikes impacting streaming chat responses. Short-term client mitigations and a remediation timeline were provided; SRE identified a batching/rate spike interaction and a rolling runtime fix was scheduled. Credits and follow-up evals were promised.
messages:
From: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@bridgeplay.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@bridgeplay.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime responses stalling during peak bursts (prod)

Hi Laura —

We started seeing a surface-level issue this morning around 08:00 PDT where users on our live chat flow see multi-second stalls during streaming responses. The UI shows the connection still open but tokens arrive in big intermittent chunks; latency for the first token appears okay but then streaming pauses for 3–8s intermittently. It started around a sudden traffic spike from a campaign.

This is impacting a handful of sessions and is reproducible if we ramp request concurrency. Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side and whether there's an immediate mitigation? We have an upcoming press demo and need short-term workarounds.

Attaching a short capture and timestamps.

Thanks,
Sarah
Senior Product Ops, BridgePlay

Attachments: bridgeplay-capture-0803.json (referenced), user-timestamps.csv

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@bridgeplay.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime responses stalling during peak bursts (prod)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick report and the captures. We're looking into this as priority. Initial notes: we are seeing elevated request concurrency and a correlated rise in token batching latency in the US-west cluster serving your traffic.

Short-term mitigations you can apply immediately (lowest friction first):
- Toggle stream -> non-stream fallback for UI-critical flows: switching to non-streaming (single response) for the demo will avoid chunked arrivals. We included a small client snippet (attached) that toggles to completion-mode and restores streaming after the spike.
- Add a short client retry/backoff: if your frontend observes >1s silence after receiving tokens, retry the request once with exponential backoff 250ms -> 500ms.
- Reduce max_concurrency on your API client from your current 40 to 15 for the demo window; this limits bursty queuing that appears to trigger batching heat-ups.

I'll set up a bridge with SRE for a deeper triage in 30 minutes; Marcus will lead the server-side investigation. We'll follow with a remediation ETA within 6 hours.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll keep you updated in this thread.

— Laura
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: streaming-fallback-client-snippets.txt

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@bridgeplay.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime responses stalling during peak bursts (prod)

On Tue, 12 Jun 2028 08:45:00 -07:00 laura_bennett@redwood.ai wrote:
> I'll set up a bridge with SRE for a deeper triage in 30 minutes; Marcus will lead the server-side investigation.

Team — triage notes from the runtime side:
- Root cause hypothesis: an interaction between the adaptive batching controller and a burst of short-sequence requests. When concurrency spikes, the controller increases batch windows to optimize throughput; combined with our KV-cache refill path and a transient lock on memory arenas, we see intermittent pauses while batches assemble.
- Repro: we reproduced at scale in a staging cluster by replaying BridgePlay's request pattern (high concurrency, many short prompts) — observed identical chunked streaming behavior.

Short-term server-side mitigations we pushed (now active on the affected nodes):
1) Reduced batching window from 12ms -> 6ms for the serving pool handling your routing tag (low risk, small costs increase).
2) Temporarily disabled the aggressive KV-cache refill on affected shards to prevent the refill lock one-thread stalls.
3) Pinned a smaller model variant to handle spikes (falls back to deterministic non-quantized model) for your routing key until the root fix is merged.

Customer impact: these changes reduced observed inter-chunk pauses from 3–8s down to <400ms in our canary runs. We left the changes live for your routing tag; you should observe smoother streaming now, but please keep the fallback guidance enabled in case of any further bursts.

Planned medium-term fix: patch to batching controller to make windowing responsive to short-sequence dominated workloads and avoid blocking KV refill paths. Target: ship in a 24h rolling runtime release and monitor for 72h.

I'll attach the incident timeline and screenshots to this thread.

— Marcus
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident-timeline.csv, streaming-triage-screenshots.zip

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@bridgeplay.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime responses stalling during peak bursts (prod) — follow-up and post-incident steps

Hi Sarah — follow-up with timeline and next steps after the triage: the temporary mitigations we applied significantly reduced streaming pauses for your traffic pattern. Key items and actions: 

What we did (recap)
- Short-term: reduced batching window, disabled aggressive KV-cache refill, pinned fallback model variant for bursts.
- Customer side: recommended lowering client concurrency and enabling non-stream fallback for demo flows; client retry snippet provided.

Why it happened
- The runtime's adaptive batching logic increased batching windows during a sudden concurrency surge. Combined with a KV-cache refill path that briefly contends on a shared allocator, this produced intermittent blocking while batches assembled.

Next steps and ETA
- SRE will ship a batching-controller patch that adapts windowing based on observed sequence-length distribution rather than raw concurrency. Target: 24 hours to rollout (Thu 14 Jun 2028 10:00 PDT).
- QA + canary: 6-hour staged canary across West clusters, full rollout dependent on canary health.
- Post-deploy verification: we'll run a replay using your traffic signature and share telemetry graphs.

Customer remediation & goodwill
- We will issue a service credit for the impacted 3-hour window (per your contract). Finance will confirm the exact credit and process within 3 business days.
- We're happy to run an optional joint postmortem call next week and walk through long-term tuning recommendations for your live-chat workloads (suggested attendees: BridgePlay engineering, Redwood SRE).

What we need from you
- If possible, keep the client non-stream fallback enabled for the demo window tomorrow morning and limit concurrency to <= 15.
- Share any additional telemetry if you see even small regressions so we can correlate quickly.

Apologies again for the interruption. We take streaming UX seriously and will push the permanent fix on the above cadence. I'll update this thread at key milestones and when the rollout completes.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

— End of thread —
